# Distributed Delivery Requirements Checklist: Real-Time Notifications

**Purpose**: PR review of requirement quality for Kafka-backed, multi-instance notification delivery.
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [../spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the required steps from backend event creation through delivery to a user's WebSocket connection specified end to end? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec define how a notification reaches a user when its active socket is connected to a different API instance than the instance processing the Kafka event? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the expected Kafka fan-out and consumer-processing semantics defined well enough to establish whether notifications may be omitted or delivered more than once across instances? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Are offline-user delivery rules explicit, including whether notifications are discarded, retained for later delivery, or replayed after reconnection? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010; User Story 1, Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the backend event categories that generate notifications, and the criteria for notifying a particular account, identified? [Gap, Spec §FR-003; Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "within a few seconds" replaced with an objective latency threshold and a defined measurement point? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec define what counts as "delivered" (for example, accepted by a server-side socket send versus acknowledged by the client)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK008 Are ordering, duplicate handling, retry behavior, and the outcome of an event that cannot be processed specified? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-011; Edge Cases]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Are the shared-event-bus and per-user-routing requirements consistent with the stated behavior for offline users and reconnection? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-009, §FR-010; User Story 1, Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK010 Do the requirements distinguish notification delivery guarantees from the separate requirement to preserve existing REST request and response behavior? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-008; User Story 2]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Are the expected concurrent connection count, event rate, and multi-instance scale boundaries quantified sufficiently to assess horizontal-scaling success? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the diagnostic fields and support outcome required by "sufficient" delivery metadata explicitly listed and objectively assessable? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-011, §SC-005; User Story 4]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for Kafka unavailability, consumer restart, and sustained backlog, including recovery or failure outcomes? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-011; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements defined for a slow or backpressured WebSocket client so its effect on notification delivery and other API requests is unambiguous? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Are notification expiry, replay boundaries, or other reconnect recovery expectations specified, or explicitly excluded from this release? [Coverage, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010; User Story 3]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK016 Are security and account-isolation requirements stated for both normal delivery and multi-instance/retry/reconnect scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005, §FR-006, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK017 Are availability or graceful-degradation expectations defined for partial Kafka or API-instance failures without weakening per-user isolation? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-009, §SC-006]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK018 Are assumptions about Kafka availability, topic ownership/configuration, and event producers documented and validated as feature dependencies? [Dependency, Assumption, Spec §FR-004; Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec identify which backend workflows produce notification events and clarify whether those events are already available or require new contracts? [Dependency, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003; Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
